applies_why: The text issues an UNDERDETERMINED verdict, one of the two verdict types whose grounds this rule restricts.
quote: UNDERDETERMINED -- answered in [CR2] §5 and [CR3] LINK 4; Mary's phrase 'thy father' is immediately qualified by the child's reference to 'my Father's business.'
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side.
room: 'never a ground' -- I weighed reading the judge's stated reasons (the rounds' answers and the passage's own qualifying phrase) as positive appeals to what the rounds and verses actually say, against reading the UNDERDETERMINED as implicitly resting on the verse's silence; the text cites content and answers, not absence, so the first reading holds.
why: The judge rests the verdict on the defender's answers in the rounds and on what Luke 2:48-49 itself says -- the qualifying reference to 'my Father's business' -- never on a claim that a single verse fails to state the link or its contrary.
